newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh port remains paralysed by strike.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh port remains paralysed by strike.

text.p: Bangladesh's main Chittagong port remained paralysed for a third day on Monday as dock workers continued an indefinite strike, port officials said.
They said nearly 22,000 dock workers walked out on Saturday in protest against handling of cargo by a private shipping firm.

Port officials said the workers were protesting against a decision by the government-run Chittagong Port Authority to allow the Bangladeshi Q.C. Shipping Ltd to use its own equipment under a privatisation policy adopted recently.
The permission was suspended in the wake of the strike but the company, owned by powerful opposition member of parliament Salahuddin Quader Chowdhury, refused to withdraw its equipment.
Chittagong City Mayor A.B.M. Mohiuddin Ahmed, a leader of the ruling Awami League, was negotiating with the strikers but with no success yet, port officials said on Monday.
They said 23 ships were stranded at the port while 17 others were halted at the outer anchorage.
"The situation has been tense with the strikers, port users and employees agitating against one another," one port official said on Monday. He gave no further details.
The port users said they were entitled, according to the port manual, to use private equipment to handle cargo if the Chittagong Port Authority (CPA) did not have appropriate equipment.
On the other hand, the Collective Bargaining Agent (CBA), supported by the workers and dockers' unions, said allowing private equipment was a "conspiracy" against workers' interest.
Meanwhile, hundreds of casual workers said they were willing to resume handling because they needed their daily wages.
Port officials warned this could trigger clashes among various groups of workers.
Chittagong Chamber of Commerce and Industry said the CBA was "illegally obstructing" the use of private equipment.
Shipping Minister A.S.M. Abdur Rab was expected to visit the port on Monday.
Captain Zahiruddin Mahmood, Chairman of the port, told Reuters: "The government will have to tackle its own labour front first to make the port run smoothly."
Officials said Bangladesh earned 2.5 billion taka by exporting these products in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June), and the current year's export target was three billion taka.
Yussuf Abdullah Harun, President of the Federation of Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry, urged the government on Monday to "solve the issue immediately".
